Bachelor of Science in Information Systems (BSIS) - 4-Year Program 2. Bachelor of Science in Criminology (BSCrim) - 4-Year Program 3. Bachelor of Science in Accounting Information Systems (BSAIS) - 4-Year Program 4. Bachelor of Science in Agriculture (BSAgri) - 4-Year Program (with Diploma in Agriculture Technology exit path after 2 years) 5. Bachelor of Arts in English Language (BAEL) - 4-Year Program 6. Bachelor of Early Childhood Education (BECEd) - 4-Year Program All degree programs are recognized by the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) and covered under Republic Act No. 10931 (Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act / Free Tuition Policy). PART 2: TPC COLLEGE ADMISSION TEST (TPCAT) & REQUIREMENTS Aspiring freshmen and transferees must undergo the TPC College Admission Test (TPCAT). Requirements for TPCAT Application: 1. Duly accomplished TPCAT Application Form 2. Certified True Copy of Form 138 (Senior High School Report Card) / Transcript of Records for Transferees 3. Certificate of Good Moral Character from previous school 4. 2 copies of 2x2 ID picture with white background 5. Photocopy of PSA Birth Certificate PART 3: ENTRANCE EXAM DAY REMINDERS & DRESS CODE Examinees must observe the following rules during the exam: 1. Bring official Examination Permit and valid ID. 2. Bring pencils (No. 2), black ballpens, and eraser. 3. Dress Code: Examinees must wear decent, respectful attire (plain white shirt or polo, decent pants/jeans, and closed shoes). 4. Strictly PROHIBITED on exam day: Ripped/tattered jeans, short shorts, sleeveless shirts, sando, crop tops, open slippers/sandals, and unauthorized electronic devices.

MORE FILIPINO STUDENTS CAN AVAIL FREE HIGHER EDUCATION WITH 27 NEWLY CHED-RECOGNIZED LUCs The Commission on Higher Education (CHED) has recognized 27 new Local Universities and Colleges (LUCs) nationwide, expanding access to free higher education under Republic Act No. 10931 or the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act. WHAT IS RA 10931? Republic Act No. 10931, signed into law on August 3, 2017, provides free tuition and exemption from other fees in state universities and colleges (SUCs), local universities and colleges (LUCs), and state-run technical-vocational institutions. KEY PROVISIONS: 1. Free Tuition: All Filipino students enrolled in SUCs and CHED-recognized LUCs are exempt from tuition fees. 2. Free Miscellaneous Fees: Students from families with a combined annual gross income of Php 400,000 or below are exempt from miscellaneous and other school fees. 3. Tertiary Education Subsidy (TES): Eligible students receive financial assistance for costs of education such as books, supplies, transportation, and personal expenses. TALIBON POLYTECHNIC COLLEGE AS A RECOGNIZED LUC: Talibon Polytechnic College (TPC) is among the CHED-recognized Local Universities and Colleges. As a recognized LUC, TPC students are entitled to: - Free tuition fees - Exemption from miscellaneous fees (for qualifying students) - Access to the Tertiary Education Subsidy program ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS: To avail of free higher education benefits, students must: - Be a Filipino citizen - Be enrolled in a CHED-recognized program - Not be a recipient of other government-funded scholarships covering tuition - Meet the income threshold for miscellaneous fee exemption (Php 400,000 combined family annual gross income) HOW TO APPLY: 1. Enroll in any CHED-recognized program at TPC 2. Submit required documents to the Registrar's Office 3. Complete the Student Assessment Form 4. For TES application, submit additional financial documents For more information, contact the CHED Regional Office or the TPC Registrar's Office.

GSIS SUBSIDY FOR SCIENCE, TECHNOLOGY, ENGINEERING, AND MATHEMATICS (GSSP) The Government Service Insurance System (GSIS) provides financial assistance to qualified dependents of GSIS members through the GSIS Subsidy for STEM Program (GSSP). PROGRAM OVERVIEW: The GSSP aims to support the education of dependents of GSIS members who are pursuing Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) courses in recognized higher education institutions. ELIGIBILITY REQUIREMENTS: 1. The applicant must be a dependent (child) of an active or retired GSIS member. 2. The applicant must be enrolled in a STEM-related course in a CHED-recognized institution. 3. The applicant must maintain a General Weighted Average (GWA) of at least 90% or its equivalent. 4. The applicant must not be more than 21 years old at the time of application. 5. The applicant must not be a recipient of any other government scholarship grant. BENEFITS: - Annual subsidy for tuition and other school fees - Book allowance - Monthly stipend APPLICATION REQUIREMENTS: 1. Accomplished GSSP Application Form 2. Certificate of Enrollment in a STEM course 3. Certified True Copy of Grades (with at least 90% GWA) 4. Birth Certificate (PSA) 5. GSIS Member's Service Record or Certification of Membership 6. 2 pcs. 2x2 ID Photo HOW TO APPLY: 1. Download the GSSP Application Form from the GSIS website (www.gsis.gov.ph) 2. Submit the accomplished form and requirements to the nearest GSIS branch 3. Wait for the evaluation and approval of your application 4. Once approved, the subsidy will be released directly to the student's school RENEWAL: - The subsidy is renewable annually, subject to the student maintaining the required GWA - Students must submit updated grades and enrollment certificate for renewal For more information, visit the nearest GSIS branch or contact GSIS through their official website at www.gsis.gov.ph.

SECTION 1. TITLE This Ordinance shall be known and cited as "Talibon Municipal Ordinance No. 127: TPC Student Boarding and Housing Regulatory Act." SECTION 2. DECLARATION OF POLICY It is the policy of the Municipal Government of Talibon to safeguard the welfare, security, moral well-being, and academic focus of students residing in boarding houses, dormitories, homestays, and apartments within the municipality, particularly those enrolled in Talibon Polytechnic College (TPC). SECTION 3. COVERAGE AND SCOPE This Ordinance covers all natural or juridical entities operating, managing, or maintaining apartments, boarding houses, dormitories, and homestay facilities within the Municipality of Talibon catering to students of Talibon Polytechnic College, especially those located within a 1-kilometer radius of the TPC campus. SECTION 4. MANDATORY PERMITS AND LICENSING No person or entity shall operate a student boarding house, apartment, or dormitory without securing the following prerequisite clearances and permits: 1. Valid Mayor's Business Permit from the LGU of Talibon. 2. Sanitary Permit and Health Certificates from the Municipal Health Office. 3. Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (FSIC) from the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP). 4. Zoning Clearance and Building Inspection Approval. 5. Registration Certificate and Joint Compliance Accreditation from the TPC Office of Student Affairs and Services (OSAS). SECTION 5. PHYSICAL AND SECURITY STANDARDS Every covered establishment must comply with the following structural and security requirements: 1. PNP AND TALIBON POLYTECHNIC COLLEGE COLLABORATE TO STRENGTHEN STUDENT SAFETY The Philippine National Police (PNP) Talibon Municipal Police Station and Talibon Polytechnic College (TPC) have joined forces to strengthen student safety through collaborative security initiatives. JOINT SAFETY INITIATIVES: 1. BOARDING HOUSE MONITORING The PNP, in coordination with TPC and the local government, conducts regular inspections of boarding houses, apartments, and dormitories near the campus. These inspections ensure compliance with Municipal Ordinance No. 127, which regulates the establishment and operation of student accommodations near TPC. Key monitoring activities include: - Verification of boarding house registration and permits - Inspection of mandatory CCTV installations - Review of logbook records for student check-in/check-out - Assessment of fire safety equipment and emergency exits - Verification of compliance with curfew regulations 2. CURFEW ENFORCEMENT The PNP enforces curfew regulations for students residing in boarding houses near the campus. Students are required to be in their respective accommodations by the designated curfew time. Violations are reported to both the boarding house operator and the TPC administration. 3. ALCOHOL AND ENTERTAINMENT PROHIBITION ZONE In compliance with Municipal Ordinance No. 127, a strict 500-meter prohibition zone around the TPC campus has been established. Within this zone: - No establishment shall sell alcoholic beverages - No entertainment establishments (karaoke bars, billiard halls) are permitted - Violations result in fines and potential closure of the establishment 4. CAMPUS SECURITY COORDINATION The PNP works closely with the TPC Chief Security Officer to: - Conduct security briefings for students during orientation - Provide rapid response for campus emergencies - Assist in enforcing the college's discipline policies when needed - Support anti-drug awareness campaigns on campus 5. STUDENT SAFETY HOTLINE A dedicated hotline has been established for students to report safety concerns, including: - Harassment or bullying incidents - Boarding house violations - Security threats - Emergency situations The collaboration between PNP and TPC aims to create a safe and conducive learning environment for the approximately 4,900 students enrolled at the college. Both institutions are committed to the holistic development and protection of the student body. This initiative is part of the broader safety framework implemented by the Local Government Unit of Talibon under the leadership of the Municipal Mayor.
